<STRUCT_0001>
Recall that a morphism of schemes <MATH_0001> is universally
injective if any base change of <MATH_0002> is injective (on underlying
topological spaces), see
Morphisms, Definition <REF_0001>.
Universally injective and unramified morphisms can be
characterized as follows.

Let <MATH_0001> be a morphism of schemes.
The following are equivalent:
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> <MATH_0002> is unramified and a monomorphism,
<STRUCT_0003> <MATH_0003> is unramified and universally injective,
<STRUCT_0004> <MATH_0004> is locally of finite type and a monomorphism,
<STRUCT_0005> <MATH_0005> is universally injective, locally of finite type, and
formally unramified,
<STRUCT_0006> <MATH_0006> is locally of finite type and <MATH_0007> is either empty
or <MATH_0008> is an isomorphism for all <MATH_0009>.
<STRUCT_0007>

We have seen in
More on Morphisms, Lemma
<REF_0001>
that being formally unramified and locally of finite type is the same thing
as being unramified. Hence (4) is equivalent to (2).
A monomorphism is certainly universally injective and
formally unramified hence (3) implies (4).
It is clear that (1) implies (3). Finally, if (2) holds, then
<MATH_0001> is both an open immersion
(Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0002>)
and surjective
(Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0003>)
hence an isomorphism, i.e., <MATH_0002> is a monomorphism. In this way we see that
(2) implies (1).

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
Condition (3) implies (5) because monomorphisms are preserved under
base change
(Schemes, Lemma <REF_0004>)
and because of the description of monomorphisms towards the spectra of fields
in
Schemes, Lemma <REF_0005>.
Condition (5) implies (4) by
Morphisms, Lemmas <REF_0006> and
<REF_0007>.

<STRUCT_0001>
This leads to the following useful characterization of closed immersions.

Let <MATH_0001> be a morphism of schemes.
The following are equivalent:
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> <MATH_0002> is a closed immersion,
<STRUCT_0003> <MATH_0003> is a proper monomorphism,
<STRUCT_0004> <MATH_0004> is proper, unramified, and universally injective,
<STRUCT_0005> <MATH_0005> is universally closed, unramified, and a monomorphism,
<STRUCT_0006> <MATH_0006> is universally closed, unramified, and universally injective,
<STRUCT_0007> <MATH_0007> is universally closed, locally of finite type, and a monomorphism,
<STRUCT_0008> <MATH_0008> is universally closed, universally injective, locally of
finite type, and formally unramified.
<STRUCT_0009>

The equivalence of (4) -- (7) follows immediately from
Lemma <REF_0001>.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
Let <MATH_0001> satisfy (6). Then <MATH_0002> is separated, see
Schemes, Lemma <REF_0002>
and has finite fibres. Hence
More on Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0003>
shows <MATH_0003> is finite. Then
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0004>
implies <MATH_0004> is a closed immersion, i.e., (1) holds.

<STRUCT_0003><STRUCT_0004>
Note that (1) <MATH_0005> (2) because a closed immersion is
proper and a monomorphism
(Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0005>
and
Schemes, Lemma <REF_0006>).
By
Lemma <REF_0007>
we see that (2) implies (3). It is clear that (3) implies (5).
